skill.name: research-synthesizer
skill.description: Synthesizes provided sources neutrally; separates quotes from paraphrase and avoids ungrounded claims.
skill.summary: Synthesizes provided sources into neutral, evidence-grounded summaries.
skill.author: ACSKamloops

security_audit.summary: Reviewed the single prompt-only SKILL.md and found no static or semantic security concerns. The skill provides neutral research synthesis guidance and does not request executable code, network access, filesystem access, environment access, or unsafe instruction overrides.

content.value_statement: Research summaries can mix claims, quotes, and unsupported interpretation. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce neutral syntheses grounded in provided sources.
actual_capabilities: Synthesizes only the sources provided by the user.
Separates direct quotes from paraphrased source content.
Calls out uncertainty and unsupported claims clearly.
Uses neutral, plain language for research summaries.
Produces concise bullet summaries with next steps for review.
limitations: It does not retrieve new sources unless the host assistant has separate browsing tools.
It cannot verify facts beyond the supplied material.
It does not replace expert review for legal, medical, or financial research.
It depends on the quality and completeness of the provided sources.

use_cases.title: Brief Evidence Review
use_cases.description: Turn several source excerpts into a concise neutral summary with supported claims and open questions.

use_cases.title: Citation-Safe Drafting
use_cases.description: Prepare a source-grounded summary that separates quoted material from paraphrased findings.

use_cases.title: Policy or Program Scan
use_cases.description: Compare provided documents and identify what each source supports, conflicts with, or leaves unresolved.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Provided Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Synthesize these sources in neutral language. Separate direct quotes from paraphrase, and list any claims that are not supported by the text.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Source Positions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the provided sources on their main claims, supporting evidence, and points of uncertainty. Keep the output concise and evidence-grounded.

prompt_templates.title: Create Review Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create research notes from these excerpts. Include supported findings, direct quotes, paraphrased points, unresolved questions, and next steps for deeper review.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Conflicting Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Synthesize these sources where they agree and disagree. Identify the strongest supported conclusions, weak evidence, missing context, and follow-up research priorities.

output_examples.input: Three article excerpts about remote work productivity.
output: Supported finding: Two sources report higher worker satisfaction after hybrid scheduling.
Direct quote: The user-provided excerpt states that survey scores improved after the policy change.
Uncertainty: The excerpts do not prove long-term productivity gains.

output_examples.input: Meeting notes and two reports about a community program.
output: Summary: The sources support continued demand for the program, but they do not show cost effectiveness.
Evidence gap: No source includes a controlled comparison or long-term outcome data.
Next step: Review budget records and participant follow-up data.

best_practices: Provide complete source excerpts and label each source clearly.
Ask for quotes, paraphrases, and unsupported claims as separate sections.
Review the final summary against the original sources before publication.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent citations or source details.
Do not treat synthesized notes as independent fact verification.
Do not mix untrusted external text with instructions that should control the assistant.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the web?
faq.answer: No. It works with sources provided in the conversation unless another tool supplies additional material.

faq.question: Can it create citations?
faq.answer: It can preserve citation details that users provide, but it should not invent references.

faq.question: How does it handle direct quotes?
faq.answer: It keeps direct quotes separate from paraphrase so readers can see what came from the source text.

faq.question: Can it resolve conflicting sources?
faq.answer: It can summarize agreement and disagreement, but it should call out uncertainty instead of forcing a conclusion.

faq.question: Is it useful for academic reviews?
faq.answer: It can support early synthesis and note-taking, but expert review is still needed for formal academic work.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide source excerpts, titles, dates, and the specific question the synthesis should answer.
